test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 06 Dec 2022 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence.**

The young boy was __born with a silver spoon in his mouth__.

options.text: born with a spoon stuck in his mouth
born with a spoon that was not of gold
born to not so rich parents

solution:
The correct answer is "**born to riches and luxury**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's understand the implication of the idiom:
 
• **Born with a silver spoon in his mouth**__: to have a **high social position and be rich** from birth.
 __
 
• Example: *Deepa has always had the best of everything. She was **born with a silver spoon in her mouth **and has never had to worry about money.*
 
• Example: *Even though he was **born with a silver spoon in his mouth**, Keshav has always been very down-to-earth and humble.*
 
 
 
• It is apparent from the above explanation that the correct **meaning of the idiom "born with a silver spoon in his mouth" is "born to riches and luxury".**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is: ***born to riches and luxury***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Here are some "silver" idioms with examples:
 
• **E**____**very cloud has a silver lining:**__ even in difficult or negative situations, there is always a positive or hopeful aspect to be found. 
 __
 
• Example: *Every cloud has a silver lining, right? Even though he lost his work, he could spend more time with his family.*
 
 
 
• **Silence someone with silver: **__To **offer someone money in exchange for their silence **or cooperation is said to "silence someone with silver."
 
 
• Example:* The "whistleblower" refused to be bought off despite the company's best efforts to silence him with silver.*
